q_exclusive_possession.text: Is exclusive possession of the premises granted to the grantee — i.e. the right to exclude all others, including the grantor?
q_exclusive_possession.legal_test: Associated Hotels of India Ltd. v. R.N. Kapoor, AIR 1959 SC 1262: the decisive test between lease and licence is whether exclusive possession is transferred. A lease transfers an interest in the property; a licence is a bare permission to use.

q_interest.text: Is the grant for a term or periodic tenancy intended to create an interest in the property (heritable/transferable), rather than a purely personal permission?
q_interest.legal_test: Section 105, Transfer of Property Act, 1882 — a lease is a transfer of a right to enjoy immovable property for a term in consideration of rent/premium. Intention to create an interest distinguishes lease from licence even where possession is exclusive.

q_indicia.text: Despite being labelled a licence, does the arrangement show indicia of exclusive possession (grantor effectively excluded, grantee controls access, long fixed term, permission for permanent structures)?
q_indicia.legal_test: Substance over form (Associated Hotels): the label is not decisive; the court looks at the substance of the rights conferred. Exclusive-possession indicia in a 'licence' pull it toward a lease.

grey_possession_no_interest.reason: Exclusive possession granted but intention to create an interest is unclear. Genuine grey zone — classification affects duty materially. Apply S.6 (highest duty of the competing descriptions) and recommend adjudication (S.31) rather than guessing.

grey_indicia.reason: A document labelled 'leave & licence' carries exclusive-possession indicia (the classic under-stamping grey zone). Substance may make it a lease. Apply S.6 highest-duty and recommend adjudication (S.31).

source.ref: Transfer of Property Act 1882 s.105; Associated Hotels of India Ltd. v. R.N. Kapoor, AIR 1959 SC 1262; Indian Stamp Act 1899 s.6
source.quoted_text: The distinction turns on transfer of exclusive possession and intention to create an interest in property (lease) versus a bare personal permission to use (licence). Where indicia conflict, s.6 charges the instrument with the highest of the competing duties.
